headword: {中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう}
reading: ちゅうしょうきぎょう

definitions.explanation: A company classified as small or medium in scale based on the number of employees and capital, as defined by Japan's Small and Medium-sized Enterprise Basic Act. In Japan, over 99% of all companies fall into this category, making the term extremely common in economic and business discussions.

examples.japanese: {中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{支援|しえん}する→支援する：25534_shiensuru⟧。
examples.english: To support small and medium-sized enterprises.

examples.english: The majority of companies in Japan are SMEs.

notes:
One of the most frequently used economic terms in Japan. {中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう} encompasses both ⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧⟦{企業|きぎょう}→企業：00225_kigyou⟧ (medium enterprises) and {小|しょう}⟦{企業|きぎょう}→企業：00225_kigyou⟧ (small enterprises), with exact thresholds varying by industry. Since over 99% of Japanese businesses qualify as SMEs and they employ around 70% of the workforce, this term appears constantly in news, policy discussions, and business contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう}⟦{支援|しえん}→支援：07778_shien⟧: SME support
- {中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう}⟦{経営|けいえい}→経営：02740_keiei⟧: SME management
- {中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう}{向|む}け: aimed at SMEs
- {中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう}{庁|ちょう}: Small and Medium Enterprise Agency
- {中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう}{診断士|しんだんし}: SME management consultant (national certification)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{大企業|だいきぎょう}→大企業：12277_daikigyou⟧: large enterprise — the counterpart term for big corporations
- ⟦{零細企業|れいさいきぎょう}→零細企業：27027_reisaikigyou⟧: micro-enterprise — even smaller than {小企業|しょうきぎょう}, typically family-run businesses with very few employees
- {ベンチャー企業|べんちゃーきぎょう}: venture company — a startup, which may be small but carries a connotation of innovation and growth potential rather than established small business
